title: Postpartum recovery
after_body: The first 6 weeks are behind you. Your body is still healing — keep up your pelvic floor exercises and be gentle with yourself.
choose_desc: Let's tailor your recovery plan to you. You can change this later.

vaginal.title: Rest and perineal care
vaginal.body: Bleeding (lochia) is heaviest in the first days. Lie down as much as you can and sleep when your baby sleeps.
tips: Rinse with warm water after every toilet visit and pat dry from front to back
Drink plenty of water — it matters for milk and recovery

vaginal.title: Gentle movement
vaginal.body: Short walks help circulation and prevent constipation. Don't lift anything heavy.
tips: Eat fiber-rich food and drink water

vaginal.title: Listening to your body
vaginal.body: Bleeding should get lighter and paler. If it suddenly increases, it may be a sign you are overdoing it.

vaginal.title: Mood and energy
vaginal.body: Lack of sleep and hormone changes affect your mood. Sadness lasting more than 2 weeks is not normal — talk to someone.
tips: Get a little fresh air every day
Share night shifts with your partner

vaginal.title: Rebuilding strength
vaginal.body: Your abdominal muscles recover slowly. Don't rush into ab workouts yet.
tips: Mind your posture, especially while breastfeeding
Do pelvic floor exercises 3 times a day

vaginal.title: 6-week checkup
vaginal.body: Your doctor's checkup shows how your recovery is going. Write down your questions in advance.
tips: Get the go-ahead to return to exercise

cesarean.title: Wound care and rest
cesarean.body: A C-section is major surgery. In the first week your main jobs are rest, pain control and keeping the incision clean and dry.
tips: Take pain relief as your doctor advised
Support your belly with a pillow when you cough
Don't lift anything heavier than your baby

cesarean.title: Wound care and light walks
cesarean.body: Walking 5–10 minutes, 2–3 times a day helps circulation. Don't lift anything heavier than your baby.
tips: Check your incision daily: redness, pus, opening
Roll onto your side to get out of bed
Plenty of water and fiber-rich food

cesarean.title: Gradually more movement
cesarean.body: As pain eases, walk a bit longer. Stairs are fine, but take them slowly.

cesarean.title: Mood and sleep
cesarean.body: Surgery and sleepless nights together can feel heavy. Asking for help is a sign of strength.

cesarean.title: Abdominal muscles
cesarean.body: The incision is closing, but the tissues inside are still healing. It's too early for ab workouts.

cesarean.title: 6-week checkup
cesarean.body: Your doctor will check your incision and overall recovery. Ask about future pregnancies and exercise.
tips: Numbness around the scar is common — ask about it
Find out when you can return to exercise

signs_question: Are you experiencing any of these?

flags.heavy_bleeding: Bleeding that soaks a pad in an hour, or large clots
flags.wound: Redness, pus or opening at the stitches
flags.leg: Swelling, redness and pain in one leg
flags.chest: Shortness of breath or chest pain
flags.headache: Severe headache that won't go away, vision changes
flags.breast: Red, hot, painful area on the breast
flags.harm: Thoughts of harming myself or my baby
flags.sad: Sadness or hopelessness lasting more than 2 weeks

urgent_body: Don't wait — call {number} now or go to the nearest hospital.
doctor_alert_body: This sign needs to be checked. Call your doctor or midwife.
harm_body: These thoughts are not your fault, and they can be treated. Call {number} now or tell someone close to you.
partner_alert_msg: I noted a worrying sign during my recovery. Please be with me / call me.
kegel_howto: Gently squeeze as if you were holding in urine. Don't hold your breath, and don't tense your belly or thighs.
kegel_note_cesarean: After a C-section, start only with your doctor's approval. Stop if you feel pain.
kegel_note: Stop if you feel pain or discomfort.
